page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-96 is a high-density general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical Intel Xeon processor cores running at a base clock frequency of 2.6 GHz, accompanied by 384.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The cache architecture features 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache pool. Hardware-assisted instructions are supported, including AVX-512 extensions (F and VNNI) alongside AES and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration flags.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute capacity across parallel execution pipelines. The system scores in the upper tier for multi-threaded performance, yielding a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 90,577.47, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 17,076.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 74,315.42. Memory bandwidth reaches 328.7 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 144.82 GB/sec for uncached writes. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect average performance levels, with a single-core Geekbench score of 1,575.0 and stress-ng single-core rating of 1,844.89, highlighting that execution gains depend on concurrent multi-core utilization.

In operational benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong throughput for data access and web delivery, recording 80.21 million Redis SET operations per second and 63.23 GB/sec in static web serving. Software compilation via Clang (50,549.0) and ray tracing (82,754.0) similarly display high processing capability. However, the system contains no dedicated hardware accelerators (0.0 GPUs), which creates a clear constraint for AI and machine learning tasks. Large-scale 70B parameter LLM text generation is restricted to 2.34 tokens per second, falling into lower benchmark percentiles due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators or discrete GPUs.

Local disk storage is not bundled (None), requiring persistence to be addressed through attached network volumes. Considering resource distribution, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiency when scaling horizontally partitioned, high-thread enterprise applications that demand substantial RAM and heavy parallel processing without GPU overhead. Suitable target deployments include large-scale web serving tiers, software build pipelines, enterprise caching layers, continuous integration services, and highly concurrent database operations.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-96 is an x86_64 general-purpose server equipped with 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) powered by Intel Xeon processors at 2.6 GHz and 384.0 GB of RAM. The instance features hardware acceleration for cryptographic workloads and AVX-512 operations, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. It delivers strong multi-core processing in benchmarks, including 90,577.47 in multi-threaded stress-ng tests, 80.21 million Redis SET operations per second, and 63.23 GB/sec static web throughput, while single-threaded tasks perform at average levels. The server does not bundle local disk storage or discrete GPUs, limiting its efficiency for large-model machine learning inference. It offers an efficient compute-to-memory balance for high-concurrency workloads, excelling in large-scale database operations, enterprise CI/CD compilation, in-memory caching systems, and heavy multi-threaded web serving.
